newsitem.title: USA: Paging Network 96 cash flow, pagers rise.
newsitem.headline: Paging Network 96 cash flow, pagers rise.

text.p: Paging Network Inc said on Thursday its consolidated operating cash flow rose to $256.8 million, a 27.7 percent increase from the $201.1 million reported last year.
The consolidated operating cash flow margins for both 1995 and 1996 were 36.4 percent.
The company said its cash flow figures were negatively impacted by the start-up of its international operations.
During the year, PageNet added 2,264,826 pagers to service for a total of 9,002,733 at the end of 1996, a 33.6 percent increase over the 6,737,907 pagers in service in 1995.

The company also said it has made "significant strides" in deploying its VoiceNow service. It plans to begin selling VoiceNow in the Dallas/Fort Worth area on February 24 and in San Francisco shortly thereafter, PageNet said.
"We are optimistic about our performance in 1997 both from our traditional paging business and VoiceNow," said Glenn Marschel, president and chief executive.
He said the company expects to expand the VoiceNow network and marketing program across the country by year-end.
"PageNet performed exceptionally well in 1996, achieving records in operating cash flow, internally generated increases in units in service and domestic operating cash flow margins," Marschel said.
He said PageNet gained domestic market share, launched its international operations and acquired additional spectrum which will help lower network capital and operating expenses.
PageNet shares were up 1-5/8 to 14-5/8 in late morning trading.
